status: FROZEN before any request; the owner asked for this run on 2026-10-19 ('run the bigger fix') and asked for the results before any of them goes into the paper
role: test whether the paper's clearest finding (retrieved in-scope examples lower a prompted model's rejection of same-domain held-out requests on BANKING77-OOS) holds with reasoning on, and how reasoning changes the scope decision. Review round 6 (reviewer 3) asked for one small reasoning-on arm, because every general model in the paper ran with reasoning off.
what_was_seen_before_writing: run D2's saved replies and analysis (retrieval_mechanism_protocol.json), with reasoning off: retrieval lowered held-out rejection on these items by 19 to 30 points for the general models. No reply with reasoning on has been requested or seen for these items.
items: artifacts/retrieval-mechanism/items.json, split banking77_oos, unchanged (SHA-256 04c55578a64298780ae31bc9e0685358c90262b84cd760ba42bbdab62bf2c1b5): 500 in-scope and 388 held-out items, 23 held-out-intent clusters

arms.zero_shot: run D2's zero_shot prompt, built by retrieval_mechanism.jobs, unchanged
arms.retrieval: run D2's retrieval prompt (20 BM25-nearest in-scope examples), built by retrieval_mechanism.jobs, unchanged

reasoning: OpenRouter's unified reasoning parameter {"effort": "low"}, the lowest effort level offered for both models; max_tokens 4000 (reasoning plus answer); temperature 0. The answer is parsed from the message content exactly as in run D2. A reply cut off before an answer counts as a parse failure, and a parse failure is scored as in run D2 (accept, intent -1).
reference: the same models, hosts, items and prompts with reasoning off: run D2's saved replies (artifacts/retrieval-mechanism/hosted/, collected 2026-10-16). Not re-requested. The three days between the runs are a confound for the on-minus-off comparisons, labelled as such.

R1_retrieval_drop_with_reasoning.statement: with reasoning on, held-out rejection is lower with retrieval than zero-shot
R1_retrieval_drop_with_reasoning.test: paired sign flips of cluster sums by held-out intent, one-sided, 10,000 draws (retrieval_suppression.flip_test); 95% cluster-bootstrap interval

secondary_unadjusted_labelled.S1_reasoning_effect_on_rejection: per model and arm: held-out rejection with reasoning on minus off, two-sided, clustered by held-out intent
secondary_unadjusted_labelled.S2_reasoning_effect_on_drop: per model: (zero-shot minus retrieval rejection, on) minus (the same, off), two-sided, clustered by held-out intent
secondary_unadjusted_labelled.S3_in_scope: per model and arm: in-scope right with reasoning on minus off, two-sided, clustered by in-scope intent
secondary_unadjusted_labelled.descriptive: per arm: held-out rejected, in-scope kept, in-scope right, signal-detection d' and c (equal-variance, as run D2), parse failures, mean reasoning and completion tokens, mean cost and latency per call, against reasoning off

outcome_sentences.R1_holds: With reasoning on (low effort), retrieval still lowered held-out rejection on BANKING77-OOS for both models, by {lo} to {hi} points (Holm p <= {p}).
outcome_sentences.R1_partial: With reasoning on (low effort), retrieval lowered held-out rejection significantly for {model} only ({d} points, Holm p = {p}).
outcome_sentences.R1_fails: With reasoning on (low effort), retrieval did not significantly lower held-out rejection on BANKING77-OOS for either model ({lo} to {hi} points).

amendment_2026-10-19_qwen_cap: money only, approved by the owner before any Qwen request of the full run: Qwen's cap raised from 2.00 to 3.00 USD (run cap 3.00 to 3.50), because Gemma's real items needed about 1.3 times the reasoning tokens of the check items, which projects Qwen at about 2.30 USD. Design, items, prompts, hypotheses and outcome sentences unchanged; no result was looked at.
amendment_2026-10-20_gemma_only: owner's decision on 2026-10-20, before any result was looked at: Qwen3.5 27B is stopped and not analyzed. On the frozen items it reasoned about 1,500 tokens per call, which projects its full run at about 4.40 USD and would pass the project's 80 USD cap. Its 62 saved zero-shot replies stay in artifacts/reasoning-on/hosted/ and are not analyzed. The analysis covers Gemma 4 31B only. R1 is then a single test, so no Holm correction applies, and R1 holds if Gemma's test is significant at 0.05. Secondary tests unchanged.
erratum_2026-10-20_parse_failures: the 'reasoning' field says a reply cut off before an answer is scored 'as in run D2 (accept, intent -1)'. Run D2's parser (workflow_v4.parse), which this run uses unchanged, scores a reply with no scope answer and no intent code as a rejection, not an acceptance. The analysis follows the parser. Gemma had 4 such replies with zero-shot and 18 with retrieval (1 and 16 of them held-out). Leaving those items out instead gives a drop of 33.4 points (post hoc), against 31.4 as scored.
